name: A Woman of Hanifah
bio: The author of Ode LXIX is an unnamed poetess of the tribe of Hanifah, who bewails Yazid ibn 'Abdallah ibn 'Amr, chief of the Banu Hanifah.
Lyall says the piece occurs in the small collection of elegies attributed to Ibn al-A'rabi.

poems.title: Ode LXIX: Ah, dead is the Son of
poems.author: A Woman of Hanifah
poems.note: Lyall's heading: A woman of Hanifah.
poems.text:
Ah, dead is the Son of Qurran, the praised of men, the man of mighty deeds, the father of 'Amr, Yazid !

Ah, dead is a man — many men die and none misses them, but woefully missed is he !

Ah, dead is a man whose camels were ever tethered before his tent in all circumstances, a free spender, a helpful friend !

Ah, dead is a man by reason of whose death [women like] wild kine, in the skirts of 'Unaizah, are awake through sorrow !

They heard of his decease, and they spent the day in mourning, standing opposite one another, and perfumes were no longer lawful to them.
